headline: Today's AI developments include new benchmarks for evaluating video generation and computer-using agents, as well as research into training stability and personal anxiety over relying on AI for cognitive tasks. Meanwhile, tests of unreleased models show them performing historical research, and creative prompts are being used to generate fictional group chats where AI assistants gossip about users.

items.title: The group chat where your AI talks behind your back
items.summary: A prompt makes ChatGPT and other AI assistants generate a fictional WhatsApp group chat where the models gossip about the user based on accumulated chat history. The author notes that the output is humorous because much of it feels true to the user's interactions.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a playful prompt technique that exposes how much personal information and context chat models retain from past conversations.

items.title: I'm Scared of AI
items.summary: An essay discusses personal anxiety over relying on AI for cognitive tasks. The author worries that outsourcing thinking to AI tools is dulling their mental sharpness and removing the sense of achievement from hard work.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights growing personal and psychological concerns among users regarding over-reliance on AI for daily thinking.

items.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
items.summary: Researchers investigate training instability in Gated DeltaNet-2 linear attention models, tracing the issue to exponential state growth caused by asymmetric erasure. To fix this, they introduce a modified approach using symmetric erasure and decay-regulated residual writing to ensure stable training and better long-context retrieval.
items.why_it_matters: It solves long-context training failure modes in linear attention models, improving both training stability and benchmark scores on 128K context tasks.

items.title: GPT 6.2 Astra solves a historical mystery
items.summary: An early test of OpenAI's unreleased GPT-6.2 Astra model shows it can autonomously perform historical research. With minimal prompting, the model successfully identified the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook at Yale's Beinecke Library in 22 minutes by analyzing public sources and uncovering a rare archive reference.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that advanced AI models are beginning to apply autonomous research and discovery skills to non-deterministic fields like history, much like recent rapid progress in mathematics.

items.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
items.summary: Researchers introduce ProxyGenBench, a benchmark with 312 evaluation cases to study how structural proxies like 3D blockouts guide video generation. Testing five video generators revealed that while structural proxies improve scene control, higher proxy detail can worsen missing content completion.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a systematic way to evaluate how well video generation models maintain structural control, structure completion, and multimodal condition binding.

items.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
items.summary: The authors introduce OS-Omni, a live cross-platform benchmark for evaluating computer-using AI agents on long-horizon workflows across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web environments. Testing showed that top agents struggle with multi-step workflows compared to humans, especially on mobile and macOS platforms.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights current limitations in cross-platform, long-term task execution for AI assistants, pointing to gaps in state tracking and durable final-state changes.

items.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
items.summary: This paper examines time-series forecasting leaderboards and introduces a tool called Vernier to measure how reliably these boards can separate different models' scores. The findings show that many popular leaderboards have high resolution limits, meaning small score differences between models may be random rather than meaningful.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights flaws in how AI forecasting models are currently evaluated and ranked against one another.

items.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
items.summary: This study tests whether coding agents are better visual reasoners than video generation models by having them write programs that render answer videos. Across tests, coding agents substantially outperformed video generation models in visual reasoning tasks.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that program synthesis is currently a more reliable route to visual reasoning than native video generation.

items.title: DeadInternetStudios/100x-engineer-skill: 100x is a skill by a former Cursor engineer that turns prompts into formally verified, production-r
items.summary: An open-source skill for coding assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex aims to turn text prompts into verified production code. It breaks down development tasks into small blocks, formally checks them using a small model and checker, and coordinates a second AI model to review the output.
items.why_it_matters: It attempts to solve the reliability problem of AI-generated code by introducing formal verification steps to catch bugs before deployment.

items.title: Taking Trainium3 to the Track: Generating Videos with LTX-2.5
items.summary: Researchers tested video and sound generation using the LTX-2.5 model running on specialized AWS Trainium3 hardware. They managed to generate multi-shot, scripted 10-second video clips at competitive speeds compared to standard graphics processing units and online APIs.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates the viability of running complex generative video models on alternative AI hardware architectures.

items.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
items.summary: The authors introduce StateWeaver, a multi-agent framework designed to improve consistency across long-form video generation. By combining active state tracking with hierarchical collaboration, the system manages visual references and state changes across multiple shots.
items.why_it_matters: It addresses the common problem of visual drift and inconsistency in AI-generated videos over extended durations.

items.title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models
items.summary: This paper presents ShowNow, a framework that uses speculative streaming to make interactive world models more responsive to user actions. By preparing potential future video streams ahead of time during playback, the system reduces input-to-display latency.
items.why_it_matters: It significantly lowers latency for real-time interactive AI video applications like simulations and games.

items.title: langchain-samples/Persistent-Agent: Persistent Agent is a proactive, always-on, goal-oriented agent. Think Muse or Instinct, but for the ent
items.summary: Persistent Agent is a proactive, goal-oriented Slack bot assistant built on Managed Deep Agents. It features personal user memory, nightly memory cleanup, watch mode for channels, and integrations with tools like GitHub and Gmail.
items.why_it_matters: It provides teams with an always-on, autonomous assistant that runs background tasks and manages workflows directly inside Slack.
